questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Toulouse was my 5th priority, so I chose it because it was in South of France.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The school was not clear on any information whatsoever. I made my study plan at home, and it seemed like I got the courses that I applied for, but when arriving I only got some of them. Due to this I had to change my entire schedule and the school did nothing to help. Further, it was impossible to know how the courses were structured. I tried to contact the school and the teachers about the dates for the mid-terms and the exams, but they didn't tell me anything until a month before the exams. The person responsible for study abroad in Toulouse did not speak English very well. The university website did not work in English so if you didn't understand french, it was almost impossible to get access to your schedule. Even some of the mid-terms where we had a multiple choice quiz the website was in french, so I did not know how to move on to the next questions. To get anything to work out with the courses was a lot of hard work because the school seemed like they didn't care or didn't want to help when you don't speak french.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: No! I would say almost impossible if you do not speak french

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an information meeting where the study guide showed how to find you schedule on a small smart phone in front of 200 people. Clear to say I could not see what she was doing

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very hard. It's a good idea to use google translate to get it in french.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a good option but I would recommend to begin the search 4-6 month a head

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The school does nothing to help. I signed up for student housing but did not get it. I tried to ask the school to help but they didn't do anything. I was lucky to find housing

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Almost everything is in french.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to meet a lot of deadlines which were extremely hard because their processing was so slow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had some student who could speak english which could help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not succesful. I did not get the classes that i originally signed up for. Then I had to find new courses which I could get transferred to my home university.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The learning agreement you have to fill out before mobility does not mean anything because the host university does not sign you up for any classes until you get there

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good professional teaching. The information about exams, mid-terms or assignments is very poor.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Good professional teaching.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Everything is on the blackboard which can get very boring sometimes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: CM Macroeconomics, Fundamentals and policies for a greener economy, Causal inference with observational data, Sustainable development, Valuing the environment and Market power and regulation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Fundamentals and policies for a greener economy, Causal inference with observational data, Sustainable development, Valuing the environment and Market power and regulation

What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I played some different kind of sports. They only speak french so it is kind of hard to participate if you cannot understand french

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: A lot of the Erasmus events are very good

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The train option are exceptional! Take a train trip to another part of France

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very hard for a person who cannot speak french

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I expected that the young people could speak English. They cannot!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It is a beautiful city which has a lot of good cafés and bars

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: They do not like to speak english so it is important to be very good in french. It is very hard to get help from the school so I would recommend to go to their office each time you have a question. Sign up for as many of the Erasmus trip as you can.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The learning agreement you fill in before is not important

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendship with people from all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That most people do not speak english

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
